content:
Hello everyone and welcome to the Cinema Slime Podcast, my name is Harrison and today we are going to be going over Season 1 Episode 5 of Spider-Man Noir entitled Betrayal. In this episode the mystery of these super powered beings is explored, Robbie stands in the spotlight as he asks the tough questions, and as the titled suggests, someone is betrayed

![image](https://image.nostr.build/07694af79bee0bcea720739b77737d167b36797309bc20ffc62c2af13f4600ac.jpg)

This is the episode where the story is shifting from the inner conflict and fleshing out of our characters and refocusing on the story of these P.O.Ws who have been cursed against their will. While the marvel universe usually explores both sides of the spectrum in terms of super powers being a blessing or a curse, this time it’s all a burden on these people.

We start out diving into the origin story of Ben Riely, a soldier in the army whose platoon was called upon to liberate an enemy occupied city in France. In the process he was able to rescue a group of P.O.Ws and discover the heinous human experiments being forced upon them. As he looks on the men being pumped full of the DNA of various animals, he is bitten by a radioactive P.O.W. who is in the midst of his final transformation into a spider. 

I think one of the greatest moments in this episode is Ben talking about how that moment effected him. We learn that the rest of the P.O.W.s that were affected have been slowly deteriorating ever since that moment, not only mentally feeling like a freak but there very lives are slipping away. Ben seems to be able to use his powers without those consequences but mentally he seems to be struggling. He talks about learning to be a human again, how he would go to the movies to learn how to talk and act and ground himself. What we saw last episode as a way from him to escape and ignores his problems all of a sudden feels significant. He just pulled off setting up Silvermane’s right hand man, barely escaping death, and him going to the movies was a way to ground himself because he felt his humanity slipping away. 

![image](https://image.nostr.build/ce7fcee39a0748ea0bdef698f971ad2f46cbd4cc1748f9d03a6bf2ae536d643b.jpg)

Throughout this episode we get to see Robbie stepping into the spotlight, selling his story of the The Spider’s fight with the ‘Conductor’ and getting his old job back felt great to see, and I think it just invigorated him even more to solve this mystery. We learn that a geneticist, Althea Faber, took a job at the VA in Queens and has been seeking out the men rescued from that town in France. She has been trying to find a cure for them but only seems to be speeding up their demise with no solution in sight. 

In the end we do another version of the same song and dance. Cat trying to escape the city, with Ben encouraging her and expressing his love to run away with her to an island where they can live out their best life. The universe always has a way to stop that. Cat’s love for Flint pushes her to find a way to save him and the key to everything is The Spider, allegedly. Dr. Faber believes that his mutation is more developed and hasn’t negatively affected him the same way as the other super powered beings. In the end, Cat gives up Ben’s name to her, and we’ll have to wait for next episode for the fallout

![image](https://image.nostr.build/e5fad848356b195cd53bad001d9786d9f0f1b84c447644f71eb61fec337cfd5b.jpg)

This episode was… fine. There’s some humorous moments, and shifting the focus to Robbie and his investigative skills was a nice change of pace. We do get the story fleshed out more inthis episode than any of the others it felt like, but it was at the cost of interesting character moments for the rest of the cast. I’ll also confess that ‘The Conductor’ really grind my gears with his long soliloquys and while it gave him a unique presence, it just felt a bit over the top. I think Silvermanes reaction to him sums him pretty well. Overall I think this was a 5/10 type of episode that pushed the story along, and sometimes you need an episode like that.
